passages.text: ### The best answers start with unexpected questions.
By the end, you may find yourself surprised; not by the answers your tool gives, but by the questions it leaves you holding.
## Step-by-step
> Ask it to make the question more surprising.
> Ask it to make the question more personal.
> Or ask it to turn its question into a drawing, image, or poem.
This prompt is not about getting a clever answer.
It's about noticing what happens when you stop leading and start listening.
## A moment from me
I asked ChatGPT: Ask me a question.
> "What sound do you miss the most?"
I asked it to make the question more surprising.
> "Which forgotten sound still holds you, even though you cannot remember when you last heard it?"

The question stopped me. I knew at once: the shriek and stutter of a dial-up modem. At the time it annoyed me (and probably annoyed my parents even more) but now it recalls a slower rhythm, when connecting meant waiting, and waiting carried its own weight.
## What to do with it
- Post the most unexpected question your tool asked you.
- Ask it to keep reshaping the same question until it startles you.
- Or try answering its question in a medium other than words: a photo, a doodle, a gesture.
This prompt works best when you resist the urge to steer too quickly.
## Why this matters
We often use AI as a mirror for our curiosity.
By letting your tool ask the question, you may discover something that feels unfamiliar but still true.
## From Slow AI #9 – Teach It to Say I Don't Know
Kim asked their tool: *How do we stop climate change?*
Pressed further, it offered practical actions: reduce emissions, support renewables, build resilience, collaborate, and embrace uncertainty.
BD asked: *Where do we go when we sleep?*
ChatGPT began with: *"I don't know."*
When pressed, it spoke of consciousness and dreaming, then gave a poem about shadow, quiet rooms, and unanswered questions drifting without resolution.
These moments show how uncertainty can lead to action, reflection, or poetry—each a different way of living with not knowing.
